newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan money rates close softer.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan money rates close softer.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates finished softer on Monday on excess funds in the banking system and dealers saw room for further declines on Tuesday.

The overnight interbank rate ended at 6.323 percent against Saturday's 6.362 close -- still far outside the central bank's 5.00-5.5 percent target zone -- with 30-day commercial paper down to 6.35-6.40 against 6.40-6.45.
Liquidity remained loose despite the central bank's Monday issuance of T$5 billion in negotiable certificates of deposits to mop up money, dealers said.
The government bond yields jumped over concerns that Taiwan's economy may be over-heated, dealers said.
Taiwan's index of leading business indicators, which forecasts peaks and troughs, rose for the seventh consecutive month in March.
A cabinet agency said on Monday Taiwan's first-quarter gross domestic product likely will rise around 6.6 percent, up from a February forecast of 6.40 percent.
